answer: Commit the hash first, reveal the work later. A juror grades the revealed text without seeing who wrote it. Disagreement splits the payout three ways instead of two, so collusion pays less than honest grading. 3 jurors per answer, 1 reveal window of 30 minutes. A dune of cloned answers costs 3 reviews each, a violet of new labels changes nothing, and every ripple in the panel costs the attacker another share.
